newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Leumi warns Israel credit rating could be hurt.
newsitem.headline: Leumi warns Israel credit rating could be hurt.

text.p: Worsening economic indicators and political instability could hurt Israel's sovereign credit rating, economists at Bank Leumi warned in a monthly report released on Monday.
The report said this could make it more expensive for Israel to raise loans abroad as well as discouraging new investment from foreigners.

"The influence of the worsening in economic indicators like external debt, the current account, the budget deficit and the slower growth rate in addition to the lack of stability in the region could hurt Israel's credit risk rating," the report said.
The current account deficit in Israel's balance of payments rose 30 percent in the first six months to $3.1 billion.

Israel's external debt rose to $20.5 billion at the end of June from $20.2 billion at the end of December and the budget deficit in the first nine months totalled 8.9 billion shekels, 20 percent more than what was targeted for the entire year.

In September Standard & Poor's and Moody's reaffirmed Israel's credit rating of A minus and A3, respectively. But since then tension has heightened in the region in the wake of bloody clashes between Palestinians and Israelis that killed more than 70 people.
Last week, the Central Bureau of Statistics forecast economic growth in 1996 at only 3.8 percent, against 7.1 percent growth last year.
Bank Leumi also warned that the recent events could lead to increased government spending on security, although the Treasury has denied this.
